verify.isa: Verify at isa.org.jm/deepdata/ — the ISA DeepData portal publishes the authoritative GIS shapefiles. Our boundaries are derived from those shapefiles; compare ISA ID numbers to confirm any claim.
verify.relinquished: Areas where contractors returned blocks to the ISA. The authoritative record is in the ISA DeepData portal at isa.org.jm/deepdata/ — compare block IDs against expired or relinquished contracts listed there. Block ID shown in the popup maps to the ISA contract reference number.
verify.reserved: Blocks reserved by coastal states under the ISA regime. Verify current status at isa.org.jm/deepdata/. Reserved area boundaries are published as part of the ISA GIS shapefiles alongside active mining contracts.
verify.apeis: Area-based Environmental Management Plan (EMP) designations established by the ISA. The full EMP documentation and APEI coordinates are at isa.org.jm/en/science/areas. Each APEI is a no-mining protected zone designed to preserve biodiversity connectivity across the Clarion-Clipperton Zone and other regions.
verify.density_intro: An equal-area hexagonal grid (~48,760 km² per cell, EPSG:6933) aggregated from all 11 underlying source tables. Verify each component at its authoritative portal:
verify.contractorStations_intro: Platform-derived rollup of contractor DwC archives ISA mirrors through OBIS. Each station's panel shows the verbatim eventID — copy that, plus the archive slug, to verify directly:
verify.contractorStations_footer: All record counts, species and phyla in the panel are platform-aggregated — not the contractor's own analysis. Verify the underlying records, not the rollup.
verify.obis_intro: Each OBIS record carries an occurrence ID. Search it at obis.org/occurrence/<id> to see the original collection event, institution, and methodology.
verify.argo: Platform IDs shown in popups can be looked up at argovis.colorado.edu. The full depth profile, quality flags, and mission metadata are available there.
verify.vents: Beaulieu, Stace E; Szafrański, Kamil M (2020): InterRidge Global Database of Active Submarine Hydrothermal Vent Fields Version 3.4 [dataset]. PANGAEA, <1>https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.917894</1>. Each vent entry includes the discovery reference.
verify.seamounts: Yesson, Chris; Letessier, Tom B; Nimmo-Smith, Alex; Hosegood, Phil; Brierley, Andrew S; Hardouin, Marie; Proud, Roland (2020): List of seamounts in the world oceans - An update [dataset]. PANGAEA, <1>https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.921688</1>. Based on SRTM v.11 bathymetry. CC BY 4.0.
verify.eez: World EEZ v12 is published by the Flanders Marine Institute (VLIZ) and hosted at marineregions.org. Cross-reference any specific boundary at marineregions.org/eez.php using the MRGID shown in the popup. Disputed boundaries are included as claimed by each state — we do not adjudicate overlapping claims.
verify.unesco: Site boundaries sourced from the UNESCO World Heritage Marine Programme layer on MarineRegions WFS. The authoritative list of all World Heritage marine sites is at whc.unesco.org/en/marine-programme/. Site polygons represent the inscribed property boundary as submitted by the nominating state.
verify.oceansites: Station metadata comes from OceanOPS — search the reference code shown in the popup at oceanops.org. For a reading, check the source the popup names for it: NDBC at ndbc.noaa.gov/station_page.php?station=REF, PMEL at data.pmel.noaa.gov/pmel/erddap, or the OceanSITES GDAC at data-oceansites.ifremer.fr. A station showing no reading cannot be cross-checked at any of those — it is in the register but not currently polled, which is a different thing from a feed that failed.
verify.currents: Cross-check current speed and direction against the Copernicus Marine viewer (product GLOBAL_ANALYSISFORECAST_PHY_001_024, dataset cmems_mod_glo_phy-cur_anfc_0.083deg_P1D-m, variables uo/vo). The source netCDF files are available for download via the Copernicus Marine Toolbox:
verify.onc: Data sourced from Ocean Networks Canada's Oceans 3.0 API at data.oceannetworks.ca. The location code shown in the popup can be used to look up the full sensor history and quality flags in the ONC Data Search portal. Sparklines (72 h) and CTD profiles come from the same API; the ADCP backscatter heatmap (24 h) is built from ONC's RADCPTS data product, with the 15-minute ensemble averaging applied by ONC. Nearby earthquake data is from the USGS FDSN Event Web Service at earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/ — cross-reference any event using the USGS event ID shown in the popup.
verify.oncInstruments: Device catalogue sourced from the ONC Oceans 3.0 instrument WFS at data.oceannetworks.ca. The device code shown in the popup can be entered in the ONC Data Search portal to view all recorded data, deployment history, and calibration logs for that specific instrument.
verify.cables: Commercial telecom routes from EMODnet Human Activities at emodnet-humanactivities.eu. Cross-reference any cable name at TeleGeography's Submarine Cable Map (submarinecablemap.com) for ownership, landing points, and capacity. ONC observatory cables are documented at oceannetworks.ca/installations. OOI RCA cables: node coordinates from github.com/oceanobservatories/asset-management; array overview at interactiveoceans.washington.edu. NOAA Marine Cadastre corridors at marinecadastre.gov (use Cable System or Owner from popup).
verify.ports: Dataset compiled from public port registries — see the source repository for provenance. Cross-reference major ports against the UN/LOCODE directory at unece.org/trade/uncefact/addressing-un-locode or the World Port Index published by the US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (Pub 150).
verify.tectonic: Peter Bird (2003) "An updated digital model of plate boundaries." Geochem. Geophys. Geosyst., 4(3). The authoritative dataset is hosted at peterbird.name/publications/2003_PB2002/2003_PB2002.htm. Public domain. Cross-reference seismicity against USGS Earthquake Hazards Program at earthquake.usgs.gov.
verify.offshore_intro: Each popup includes a direct link to the authoritative registry for that jurisdiction. Cross-reference independently at the portals below — the registry ID shown in the popup ("Registry ID" field) maps to the licence number in the source system.
verify.noiseRisk: Impulsive noise (Pulse Block Days) from ICES Registry at gis.ices.dk — search "CEMP PulseBlockDays". Continuous SPL from EMODnet Physics at emodnet-physics.eu. Cetacean sightings from OBIS-SEAMAP at seamap.env.duke.edu. Risk index formula: (pbd_norm or spl_norm) × cetacean_norm × IUCN species weight, capped at 1.0 (MSFD Descriptor 11 methodology). A modeled index, not a measurement.
verify.chess: Source: gbif.org/dataset/dc5abc9f-84d5-4046-a3ef-9ab24ae53756. Each record carries a species name, taxonomy, depth, locality and institution from ChEssBase via GBIF, passed through unchanged. ⚠️ A `habitat_type` field used to appear here — our own keyword classification of the free-text locality. It was removed on 2026-09-21, because ChEssBase publishes no habitat field at all: the Darwin Core terms that could carry one (`habitat`, `waterBody`, `occurrenceRemarks`, `samplingProtocol`) are empty in every record we sampled. Every value in that column was our claim wearing the source's clothes, and it was wrong in both directions — 97% of records fell through to Unclassified, while Blake Ridge, a gas-hydrate seep province, was labelled a vent because its name contains the word "ridge". Nothing replaces it: read the habitat from the species list, which is the actual evidence.
verify.worms: Copy the AphiaID from any verified species panel and look it up at marinespecies.org to confirm the accepted name and classification.
verify.landMining: Maus, Victor; da Silva, Dieison M; Gutschlhofer, Jakob; da Rosa, Robson; Giljum, Stefan; Gass, Sidnei L B; Luckeneder, Sebastian; Lieber, Mirko; McCallum, Ian (2022): Global-scale mining polygons (Version 2) [dataset]. PANGAEA, <1>https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.942325</1>. Sentinel-2 derived polygons at 10m resolution. CC BY 4.0. Companion paper: Maus et al. (2022) Sci. Data 9, 433.
verify.kba: World Database of Key Biodiversity Areas at keybiodiversityareas.org. Managed by BirdLife International on behalf of the KBA Partnership (12 international conservation organisations). KBA criteria follow the IUCN Global Standard (2016). Site assessments are peer-reviewed.
verify.tailings: Base locations: Hudson-Edwards, K. et al. (2023) WAPHA global metal mines database at doi.org/10.5061/dryad.j3tx95xmg (CC0), mirrored at zenodo.org/records/8324697 (11,587 facilities). Global Tailings Portal (GRID-Arendal, tailing.grida.no) hazard/ownership fields are withdrawn pending written permission (decided 2026-09-23) and are not served.
verify.fires: NASA LANCE FIRMS at firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov. Verify any detection by searching its coordinates in the FIRMS map viewer, matching on date, time and satellite. VIIRS V2 algorithm, near-real-time product. Data is public domain (US Government work).
verify.airQuality: OpenAQ at openaq.org. Aggregates government reference-grade monitors — not low-cost sensors. Each station links back to its national monitoring network. Verify readings against the original source network for regulatory purposes. CC BY 4.0.
verify.landslides: NASA COOLR at coolr.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov. Cooperative Open Online Landslide Repository compiled by NASA Goddard. Events sourced from news, government reports, and citizen science (Landslide Reporter app). Each record includes a source URL for verification.
verify.dams: Global Dam Watch v1.1 at www.globaldamwatch.org. Combines ICOLD World Register, GRanD, GOODD, and national inventories. Lehner et al. (2011) for GRanD; Mulligan et al. (2020) for GOODD. CC BY 4.0.
verify.surfaceWater: JRC Global Surface Water at global-surface-water.appspot.com. Pekel et al. (2016) "High-resolution mapping of global surface water and its long-term changes." Nature 540, 418–422. Derived from 4.7 million Landsat scenes. Tiles served from Google Earth Engine. Public domain (EC/JRC).
verify.waterRisk: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 at wri.org/aqueduct. Hofste et al. (2019) "Aqueduct 3.0: Updated Decision-Relevant Global Water Risk Indicators." 68,506 sub-basin polygons (HydroBASINS × GADM × WHYMAP) with 13 water risk indicators. Mining-weighted composite uses industry-specific weights for water stress, depletion, drought, and flood risk. CC BY 4.0.
verify.treeCoverLoss: Global Forest Watch at globalforestwatch.org/map. Hansen/UMD/Google/USGS/NASA annual tree cover loss product (30 m, 2000–present). Verify annual loss figures or download the underlying rasters at earthenginepartners.appspot.com/science-2013-global-forest. CC BY 4.0.
verify.forestCarbon: Global Forest Watch Climate at globalforestwatch.org/topics/climate. Harris et al. (2021) “Global maps of twenty-first century forest carbon fluxes.” Nature Climate Change 11, 234–240, DOI: 10.1038/s41558-020-00976-6, revised by Gibbs et al. (2025). Net emissions and removals at 30 m, 2001–2025, dataset gfw_forest_carbon_net_flux v20250430. CC BY 4.0.
verify.soilCarbon: ISRIC — SoilGrids at soilgrids.org. Global soil organic carbon content, top 0–5 cm (soc_0-5cm_mean), ~250 m resolution, produced by ISRIC — World Soil Information using machine learning on global soil profile and environmental covariate data. Download and methodology at soilgrids.org. CC BY 4.0.
verify.lim_obis: Species occurrence layers (OBIS, ChEssBase) reflect reported observations, not total distribution — unsampled areas may harbour undiscovered species
verify.lim_vents: Vent status (confirmed / inferred / inactive) reflects the last published survey — confirmed means directly observed, inferred means deduced from a plume or chemical anomaly; vents are rarely revisited
verify.lim_argo: Argo float positions are last known locations; floats drift continuously
verify.lim_isa: ISA block boundaries are exploration zones, not guaranteed mining footprints
verify.lim_conflict: Conflict risk levels are spatial proximity assessments, not legally binding determinations
verify.lim_oceansites: Readings are fetched only for moorings OceanOPS currently lists as operational — around 60 of roughly 1,070 stations. Every other ring shows position and metadata only, and NDBC in practice supplies none of the current readings even though it is tried first
verify.lim_onc: ONC shows the most recent reading it holds for each station, with no recency floor — a retired node or a recovered drifter can show a reading that is years old, so read the timestamp beside the value
verify.lim_noise: Noise Risk cells marked 'data gap' have measured noise but no cetacean survey coverage — absence of records does not mean absence of animals
verify.lim_chess: Chemosynthetic Sites habitat type is keyword-inferred from locality names — records with non-descriptive names default to OMZ; manual reclassification is not possible without authoring new OBIS records
verify.lim_miningFootprints: Mining Footprints are satellite-classified — false positives exist in barren/urban terrain; underground mines are invisible
verify.lim_kba: KBA assessment coverage is uneven globally — well-assessed in Europe/Americas, significant gaps in Central Asia and some island states
verify.lim_tailings: Tailings dam locations are registry-compiled points from WAPHA — name, location and country only. Global Tailings Portal enrichment (hazard rating, ownership, dam specifications) is withdrawn pending permission from GRID-Arendal. Many Chinese entries are generic ('尾矿库').
verify.lim_fires: FIRMS fire detection misses fires under cloud cover and may flag industrial heat sources (smelters, gas flares) as false positives
verify.lim_airQuality: Air quality station density is highly uneven — Europe and North America are well-covered; sub-Saharan Africa has large monitoring gaps
verify.lim_landslides: Landslide catalogue is biased toward populated areas — remote events are underreported; submarine landslides are excluded
verify.lim_dams: Dam coordinates are point centroids, not dam crest footprints — small run-of-river weirs below the height threshold are excluded
verify.lim_surfaceWater: Surface Water is a 37-year composite (1984–2021) — it shows historical occurrence frequency, not current water level
verify.obis_citation: Citation: OBIS ({{year}}) Deep-sea species occurrence records (depth ≥ 50 m). Available: Ocean Biodiversity Information System. Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO. https://obis.org.
verify.reportText: If you find a factual error or stale data, the source repositories above are the place to report it. Data corrections flow into this map at the next sync cycle.
